liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews, 2 other sources): The unknown vocalist keeps up odd contributions, harmonica included, through Not Fade Away into Lovelight; The reviewer started laughing at the interloper's antics about halfway through Not Fade Away [1][3][11][14]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): By Lovelight, perhaps 50 audience members were on stage with the band, surrounding the musicians [9]
- **Inpromptu Blues** (1 review): The guest sounded decent in the blues jam that grew out of Katie Mae, riling the crowd while the band followed [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Katie Mae**: rare: 10 archived performances [18]
- **blues jam**: back after 150 archived shows (494 days); rare: 5 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd70-03-08.sbd.9195.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 15 songs; 92 min; rated 3.45/5 by 20 [1]
- **gd1970-03-08.sbd.unk.13191.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 93 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1970-03-08.145952.sbd.knudsen.markson.sirmick.flac24**: soundboard; 15 songs; 94 min [4]. Said about its sound: This version sounds much more in your face than the other three circulating sources [4]
- **gd1970-03-08.sbd.miller.113359.flac16**: soundboard; 15 songs; 92 min; rated 3.36/5 by 14 [2]

## Around the show

- After Hard to Handle the band paused and went acoustic, then returned to electric for the impromptu blues with an unknown singer [1]
- After Hard to Handle the band paused and went acoustic, then returned to electric for the impromptu blues with an unknown singer [3]
- A bizarre, apparently intoxicated stage guest made parts of the show more comedic than musical [6]
- A person allowed onto the stage nearly ruined the performance, according to this listener [7]
- Reviewer names the stage vocalist as Wayne "The Harp" Ceballos, whose vocal contributions were fairly common in that era [8]
- Attendee says the singer was an audience member in a long overcoat who climbed onstage, and the band backed him [9]
- The Star Theatre had a round revolving stage; it is now Celebrity Theatre, at 32nd St. and Van Buren [9]
- The playing is hot, but an intruder joins in and nearly ruins it; reviewer found it funny [11]
- A Santa Monica Civic tape long circulated as 3/8/70 is actually from 3/7/70, according to deadlists.com [4]
- Compares to 8/23/69, which also features Ceballos, plus Charles Lloyd; this reviewer thinks the show is a hot example [8]
- Reviewer is surprised such stage interruptions did not happen more often given how many shows the band played [11]
- Compares the stage guest's singing with Lovelight on 6/8/69, where Ceballos handles all vocals, noting differences and similarities [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-03-08.sbd.9195.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1970-03-08.sbd.unk.13191.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by theotherwayne; source: SBD>?>DAT>CDR [3]. Also: Latvala reports two vault reels carry this date; the second is blank, and the first holds this content [3]
- **gd1970-03-08.145952.sbd.knudsen.markson.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Jeff Knudson; transferred by Tom Markson and Sirmick; source: Source: sbd > ??? >cassette (high gen, from The Knudsen Collection at Lossless Legs) [4]. Also: A mastered copy of shnid 145934, with most hiss and some 60Hz hum removed [4]
- **gd1970-03-08.sbd.miller.113359.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [2]
